explanation:
[EFFECT]
Wind speed has a mostly negative effect on predicted bike demand, and the impact grows stronger as wind speed increases. At low wind speeds (roughly below 13 km/h), the contribution is near zero or very slightly positive. Beyond about 20 km/h, demand is increasingly suppressed, with the contribution falling to around −0.35 in log space at the highest observed speeds (around 54 km/h), meaning demand could be reduced by roughly 30% compared to calm conditions.

[IMPORTANCE]
Wind speed is ranked 8th out of 9 features in terms of importance (importance score = 0.014), making it one of the weakest drivers of predicted demand in the model. Its overall influence is modest compared to factors like hour of day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION]
On days forecast to have high winds (above roughly 40–50 km/h), operators can expect slightly lower ridership and may consider deploying fewer bikes or adjusting staff levels accordingly, though the effect is small relative to other factors.
